correctness.rationale: For n>=3 a CDS has at least n-1 original vertices, since two omissions force an isolated subdivision vertex. All-original selections fail inclusion-minimality by deleting a selected cycle subdivision vertex or a leaf original vertex of a spanning tree. With exactly one omission v, minimality forces a spanning tree among remaining originals and exactly one subdivided incident edge to dominate v. Every constructed set is minimal against all proper CDS subsets because each remaining original and each selected subdivision vertex is forced by connectivity or domination. Cayley counts (n-1)^(n-3) spanning trees, giving n(n-1)^(n-2) configurations of size 2n-2. Brute-force verification covers 2,131,004 nonempty subsets for n=3..6; all generated n=7 examples pass direct checks. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family, simultaneously full once-subdivisions and central graphs of complete graphs, receives a complete all-minimal-solution classification, exact Cayley-type enumeration and equality of lower/upper connected domination. The bijection with a deleted vertex, selected incident edge and arbitrary labelled spanning tree makes the solution space explicit rather than merely reporting a minimum size. This exact classification is mathematically motivated by hard general minimal-CDS enumeration and is not an arbitrary finite slice or a textbook parameter substitution.
